review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

18:1.sourceText: Ἔλεγεν δὲ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ δεῖν πάντοτε προσεύχεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ μὴ ἐνκακεῖν,
18:1.targetText: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart:

groups.note: The article τό makes the infinitive δεῖν ("to be necessary") a noun, rendered "need".
αὐτούς, the subject of προσεύχεσθαι ("to pray"), is rendered by the possessive "their".

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb.

18:2.sourceText: λέγων Κριτής τις ἦν ἔν τινι πόλει τὸν Θεὸν μὴ φοβούμενος καὶ ἄνθρωπον μὴ ἐντρεπόμενος.
18:2.targetText: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.

groups.note: The participle φοβούμενος ("fearing") is rendered as the clause "who ... feared".
καὶ ... μή ("and not") is rendered "nor".

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:3.sourceText: χήρα δὲ ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσα Ἐκδίκησόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου μου.
18:3.targetText: And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’

groups.note: BSB turns "and she kept coming" (imperfect ἤρχετο) into the relative clause "who kept appealing".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts "and she kept coming" as the relative clause "who kept appealing", so καί has no separate English word.
The participle λέγουσα ("saying") is represented only by the comma before the quotation.

18:4.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἐπὶ χρόνον· μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ Εἰ καὶ τὸν Θεὸν οὐ φοβοῦμαι οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπον ἐντρέπομαι,
18:4.targetText: For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men,

groups.note: οὐκ ἤθελεν ("he was not willing") is rendered "refused".
μετὰ ταῦτα ("after these things") is rendered "later".
Εἰ καί ("even if") is concessive, rendered "Though".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the opening καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:5.sourceText: διά γε τὸ παρέχειν μοι κόπον τὴν χήραν ταύτην ἐκδικήσω αὐτήν, ἵνα μὴ εἰς τέλος ἐρχομένη ὑπωπιάζῃ με.
18:5.targetText: yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Then she will stop wearing me out with her perpetual requests.’”

groups.note: διὰ τό with the infinitive gives the reason, "because".
παρέχειν ... κόπον ("to cause trouble") is rendered "keeps pestering".
ἵνα ("so that") introduces the outcome, which BSB states as a new sentence beginning "Then".
μή with the present subjunctive ("not keep on") is rendered "stop".
εἰς τέλος ("to the end", "continually") is rendered "perpetual".
The participle ἐρχομένη ("coming") is rendered "with her ... requests".
ὑπωπιάζῃ (literally "strike under the eye") means "wear out"; "she will" goes with this verb and "stop" with μή.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:6.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος Ἀκούσατε τί ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀδικίας λέγει·
18:6.targetText: And the Lord said, “Listen to the words of the unjust judge.

groups.note: τί ... λέγει ("what ... says") is rendered "the words of".
The genitive τῆς ἀδικίας ("of unrighteousness") is rendered by the adjective "unjust".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:7.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, καὶ μακροθυμεῖ ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς;
18:7.targetText: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He continue to defer their help?

groups.note: The emphatic negative οὐ μή, in a question expecting the answer yes, is rendered "not"; "Will" goes with the verb.
The present μακροθυμεῖ ("is he slow to act") is rendered "continue to defer".
ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς ("over them") is rendered by the possessive "their".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render δέ here.
BSB starts a second question instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "defer".

18:8.sourceText: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν αὐτῶν ἐν τάχει. πλὴν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐλθὼν ἆρα εὑρήσει τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
18:8.targetText: I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?”

groups.note: ἐν τάχει ("in quickness") is rendered "promptly".
The participle ἐλθών ("having come") is rendered as a when-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render ὅτι ("that") here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The particle ἆρα marks a doubtful question, which English shows by word order.

18:9.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ πρός τινας τοὺς πεποιθότας ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι εἰσὶν δίκαιοι καὶ ἐξουθενοῦντας τοὺς λοιποὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην.
18:9.targetText: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:

groups.note: δίκαιοι ("righteous"), in the clause "that they were righteous", is rendered by the noun "righteousness".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
BSB recasts ὅτι εἰσίν ("that they were") with δίκαιοι as the noun phrase "their own righteousness", so these words have no separate English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:10.sourceText: Ἄνθρωποι δύο ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσεύξασθαι, ὁ εἷς Φαρισαῖος καὶ ὁ ἕτερος τελώνης.
18:10.targetText: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

18:11.sourceText: ὁ Φαρισαῖος σταθεὶς ταῦτα πρὸς ἑαυτὸν προσηύχετο Ὁ Θεός, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὥσπερ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἅρπαγες, ἄδικοι, μοιχοί, ἢ καὶ ὡς οὗτος ὁ τελώνης·
18:11.targetText: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like the other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ταῦτα ("these things"), the object of προσηύχετο, untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle σταθείς, rendered "stood", to "prayed".

18:12.sourceText: νηστεύω δὶς τοῦ σαββάτου, ἀποδεκατεύω πάντα ὅσα κτῶμαι.
18:12.targetText: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’

groups.note: The genitive τοῦ σαββάτου ("of the week") is rendered "a week".
BSB's Greek has another form of this verb with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two clauses; the Greek has no conjunction.

18:13.sourceText: ὁ δὲ τελώνης μακρόθεν ἑστὼς οὐκ ἤθελεν οὐδὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπᾶραι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἀλλ’ ἔτυπτεν τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ λέγων Ὁ Θεός, ἱλάσθητί μοι τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ.
18:13.targetText: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’

groups.note: οὐκ ἤθελεν ("he was not willing") is rendered "unwilling".
οὐδέ ("not even") supplies "even"; its negative is already in "unwilling".
The article τούς has possessive force here.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English renders the participle λέγων ("saying") as a second finite verb joined by "and".

18:14.sourceText: λέγω ὑμῖν, κατέβη οὗτος δεδικαιωμένος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ παρ’ ἐκεῖνον· ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
18:14.targetText: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

groups.note: εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ("to his house") is rendered "home".
The pronoun ἐκεῖνον ("that one") is rendered "the Pharisee".

18:15.sourceText: Προσέφερον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ βρέφη ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅπτηται· ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτοῖς.
18:15.targetText: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered with the name Jesus.
The article τά has possessive force here.
ἅπτηται αὐτῶν ("He might touch them") is rendered "Him to place His hands on them".
The participle ἰδόντες ("having seen") is rendered as a when-clause.
BSB identifies αὐτοῖς ("them") as the people who brought the babies.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the impersonal plural Προσέφερον.
English supplies the object of "saw".
English adds this clause to make clear whom the disciples rebuked.

18:16.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὰ λέγων Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά· τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ.
18:16.targetText: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

groups.note: προσεκαλέσατο ("called to himself") is rendered "called ... to Him".
The pronoun αὐτά ("them") is rendered "the children".
The possessive genitive τοιούτων ("of such ones") after ἐστίν is rendered "to such as these".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English renders the participle λέγων ("saying") as a second finite verb joined by "and".

18:17.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.
18:17.targetText: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

groups.note: The double negative οὐ μή is rendered "never".
English transitive "enter" absorbs εἰς ("into").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:18.sourceText: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησέν τις αὐτὸν ἄρχων λέγων Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
18:18.targetText: Then a certain ruler asked Him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

groups.note: BSB recasts the participle ποιήσας ("having done") as the main verb "must I do".
BSB recasts the main verb κληρονομήσω ("shall I inherit") as the purpose "to inherit".

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the comma and quotation marks.

18:19.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ Θεός.
18:19.targetText: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.

groups.note: εἰ μή ("if not") is rendered "except".
εἷς ("one") is rendered "alone".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

18:20.sourceText: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
18:20.targetText: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”

groups.note: Μή with the aorist subjunctive is a prohibition; English "do" goes with the verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:21.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητος.
18:21.targetText: “All these I have kept from my youth,” he said.

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here; N1904 has no possessive with νεότητος.

18:22.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἔτι ἕν σοι λείπει· πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ διάδος πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
18:22.targetText: On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered "On hearing".
ἕν σοι λείπει ("one thing is lacking to you") is recast with "You" as the subject of "lack".
πάντα ὅσα ("all that") is rendered "everything".
The dative plural πτωχοῖς ("to poor people") is rendered "to the poor".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "hearing".

18:23.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας ταῦτα περίλυπος ἐγενήθη, ἦν γὰρ πλούσιος σφόδρα.
18:23.targetText: But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.

groups.note: The article ὁ ("he") is rendered "the ruler".
The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered as a when-clause.

18:24.sourceText: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσπορεύονται·
18:24.targetText: Seeing the man’s sadness, Jesus said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered "the man's".
The adverb δυσκόλως ("with difficulty") is recast as "hard it is for".
οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες ("those who have wealth") is rendered "the rich".
English transitive "enter" absorbs εἰς ("into"); the present "are entering" is recast as an infinitive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with extra words here that N1904 lacks.

18:25.sourceText: εὐκοπώτερον γάρ ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρήματος βελόνης εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.
18:25.targetText: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

groups.note: τρῆμα ("hole") is rendered by the English idiom "the eye" of a needle.
εἰσελθεῖν ("to enter") is rendered "pass" with "through".
English transitive "enter" absorbs εἰς ("into").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:26.sourceText: εἶπαν δὲ οἱ ἀκούσαντες Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;
18:26.targetText: Those who heard this asked, “Who then can be saved?”

groups.note: καί at the head of the question ("and who ...?") is rendered "then".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "heard".

18:27.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Τὰ ἀδύνατα παρὰ ἀνθρώποις δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἐστιν.
18:27.targetText: But Jesus said, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he", which BSB names as Jesus.
Τὰ ἀδύνατα ("the impossible things") is rendered as the clause "What is impossible".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula of the clause "What is impossible".

18:28.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφέντες τὰ ἴδια ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι.
18:28.targetText: “Look,” said Peter, “we have left all we had to follow You.”

groups.note: The participle ἀφέντες ("having left") is rendered as the main verb "have left".
τὰ ἴδια ("our own things") is rendered "all we had".
BSB recasts ἠκολουθήσαμεν ("we followed") as the purpose "to follow".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:29.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ γονεῖς ἢ τέκνα ἕνεκεν τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ,
18:29.targetText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he", which BSB names as Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") implicit.
BSB does not render ὅτι, which introduces the quoted statement.
BSB recasts "there is no one who" as "no one who", so ἐστιν ("is") has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:30.sourceText: ὃς οὐχὶ μὴ λάβῃ πολλαπλασίονα ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
18:30.targetText: will fail to receive many times more in this age—and in the age to come, eternal life.”

groups.note: The double negative οὐχὶ μή after "no one" in 18:29 is rendered "fail to".
BSB's Greek has another form of this verb with the same meaning.
The article with the participle (τῷ ἐρχομένῳ, "the coming one") is rendered "to come".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes "no one who has left" in 18:29 the subject of "will fail", so the repeated relative ὅς ("who") has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:31.sourceText: Παραλαβὼν δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱερουσαλήμ, καὶ τελεσθήσεται πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τῷ Υἱῷ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
18:31.targetText: Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.

groups.note: The participle Παραλαβών ("taking along") is rendered as the finite verb "took ... aside".
BSB recasts the passive τὰ γεγραμμένα ("the things written") through the prophets as "the prophets have written".
The dative τῷ Υἱῷ ("for the Son") is rendered "about the Son".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the prophets the subject of "have written", so διά ("through") has no separate English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle and verb.
English joins the participle Παραλαβών, rendered "took", to "said".

18:32.sourceText: παραδοθήσεται γὰρ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαιχθήσεται καὶ ὑβρισθήσεται καὶ ἐμπτυσθήσεται,
18:32.targetText: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and does not render γάρ ("for").

18:33.sourceText: καὶ μαστιγώσαντες ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ ἀναστήσεται.
18:33.targetText: They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again.”

groups.note: The participle μαστιγώσαντες ("having flogged") is rendered as a finite verb sharing "They will".
The one αὐτόν ("him") is the object of both verbs; BSB repeats "Him".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence with "They" instead of rendering καί.
The repeated article τῇ with τρίτῃ is covered by the single "the".

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle μαστιγώσαντες, rendered "flog", to "kill".

18:34.sourceText: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐδὲν τούτων συνῆκαν, καὶ ἦν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο κεκρυμμένον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον τὰ λεγόμενα.
18:34.targetText: But the disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοί ("they") is rendered "the disciples".
οὐδέν ("nothing") is rendered "not ... any".
τὰ λεγόμενα ("the things being said") is rendered "what He was saying".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering καί.
BSB renders τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο ("this saying") as "The meaning", without "this".

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the speaker; the passive participle λεγόμενα names none.

18:35.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἐγγίζειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱερειχὼ τυφλός τις ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἐπαιτῶν.
18:35.targetText: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal "as".
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered with the name Jesus.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.

18:36.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ ὄχλου διαπορευομένου ἐπυνθάνετο τί εἴη τοῦτο.
18:36.targetText: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered as a When-clause.
εἴη τοῦτο ("this might be") is rendered "was happening".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

18:37.sourceText: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται.
18:37.targetText: “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by,” they told him.

groups.note: ὁ Ναζωραῖος ("the Nazarene") is rendered "of Nazareth".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
ὅτι introduces the report, which BSB gives as direct speech.

18:38.sourceText: καὶ ἐβόησεν λέγων Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ Δαυείδ, ἐλέησόν με.
18:38.targetText: So he called out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων ("saying") only introduces the quotation.

18:39.sourceText: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ ἵνα σιγήσῃ· αὐτὸς δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν Υἱὲ Δαυείδ, ἐλέησόν με.
18:39.targetText: Those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

groups.note: ἵνα with the subjunctive is rendered as an infinitive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the opening καί.

18:40.sourceText: σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι πρὸς αὐτόν. ἐγγίσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν
18:40.targetText: Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had been brought near, Jesus asked him,

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered "the man".
The genitive absolute ἐγγίσαντος αὐτοῦ ("when he had come near") is rendered "When he had been brought near".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle σταθείς, rendered "stopped", to "directed".
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb.

18:41.sourceText: Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Κύριε, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.
18:41.targetText: “What do you want Me to do for you?”  “Lord,” he said, “let me see again.”

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he".
ἵνα with the subjunctive voices the request, rendered "let".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

18:42.sourceText: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀνάβλεψον· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
18:42.targetText: “Receive your sight!” Jesus replied. “Your faith has healed you.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the opening καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit.

18:43.sourceText: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ δοξάζων τὸν Θεόν. καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἰδὼν ἔδωκεν αἶνον τῷ Θεῷ.
18:43.targetText: Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people who saw this gave praise to God.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("him") is rendered with the name Jesus.
The participle ἰδών ("having seen") is rendered as the clause "who saw".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the opening καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "saw".
